market_pulse.note: Closed Tuesday at about 52,231, down 0.3%, after Monday's 2.15% gain to 52,389.75.
Closed Tuesday at about 7,520, down 0.4%, trimming a midday loss of roughly 0.9%.
Closed Tuesday at about 25,065, down 0.7%, the weakest of the three major indexes as tech led the decline.
December WTI traded near $86.37 a barrel late Tuesday morning, down about 0.6% from Monday's $86.85 settlement, as prices hovered near their lowest since August.

themes.title: October CPI runs hotter than expected
themes.summary: Consumer prices rose 0.4% in October versus 0.3% expected, and core prices rose 0.3%, renewing concerns about inflation.

themes.title: December Fed hike odds firm up
themes.summary: Futures traders price about 90% odds of a quarter-point hike in December and about 10% odds of a half-point move; Governor Waller said a hike of at least 25 basis points is warranted.

themes.title: Treasury yields jump
themes.summary: The 10-year yield rose about 12.6 basis points to roughly 4.99% and the 2-year about 18.9 basis points to roughly 4.74%, both the highest since late October.

themes.title: Nvidia drags on tech
themes.summary: Nvidia fell 5.5%, the Dow's worst performer for a second straight session, amid a board inquiry involving CEO Jensen Huang; the stock is down nearly 30% since early October.

themes.title: Anthropic sets IPO terms
themes.summary: Anthropic plans to sell 825 million shares at $70 to $78 each, which would raise more than $64 billion at the top of the range and value the company at about $1.4 trillion.

sectors.name: Semiconductors / AI
sectors.note: Led the decline as higher yields weighed on growth stocks; Nvidia fell 5.5%, and Intel and Marvell were lower before the open.

sectors.name: Financials / Energy
sectors.note: Held up best in early trading, each down 0.2% or less as of 10:30 a.m. ET.

sectors.name: Materials / Industrials / Utilities
sectors.note: Among the weakest groups in early trading, each down about 0.7% to 0.8% as of 10:30 a.m. ET, after industrials led Monday's rally.

sectors.name: Small Caps
sectors.note: The Russell 2000 closed down about 0.6%, recovering from a 1% drop in morning trading.

watch_list.why: AI-infrastructure results are a test for AI-linked stocks; CoreWeave and Nebius fell more than 4% before the open ahead of the report.
The bond market is closed Wednesday, while stocks trade normally.
Shares could begin trading as early as next week, though no date has been set.
